text:
Predicates:
Supervised(x) ::: x is a supervised learning algorithm.
Unsupervised(x) ::: x is an unsupervised learning algorithm.
Reinforcement(x) ::: x is a reinforcement learning algorithm.
RequiresLabelledData(x) ::: x requires labelled data.
Trains(model, algorithm) ::: algorithm is used to train model.
StateOfTheArt(model) ::: model is the state-of-the-art text summarization model.
MLAlgorithm(x) ::: x is a machine learning algorithm.

Premises:
∀x (MLAlgorithm(x) → (Supervised(x) ∨ Unsupervised(x) ∨ Reinforcement(x))) ::: Machine Learning algorithms can be categorized as supervised learning, unsupervised learning, and reinforcement learning.
∀x (Unsupervised(x) → ¬RequiresLabelledData(x)) ::: Unsupervised learning doesn't require labelled data.
StateOfTheArt(textSumModel) ::: The state-of-the-art text summarization model is trained with machine learning algorithms.
∃x (MLAlgorithm(x) ∧ Trains(textSumModel, x)) ::: The state-of-the-art text summarization model is trained with machine learning algorithms.
¬∃x (Reinforcement(x) ∧ Trains(textSumModel, x)) ::: Reinforcement learning is not used to train the state-of-the-art text summarization model.
∀x (Trains(textSumModel, x) → RequiresLabelledData(x)) ::: The Machine Learning algorithm for training text summarization model requires labelled data.

Conclusion:
∃x (Supervised(x) ∧ Trains(textSumModel, x)) ::: Supervised learning is used to train the state-of-the-art text summarization model.
